findings.problem: fs::read_to_string(path).unwrap() panics on I/O failure (missing file, permission denied, oversized file)
findings.failure_mode: untrusted or absent file path aborts the entire program instead of returning a typed I/O error
findings.fix: return Result<Vec<Record>, std::io::Error> and propagate with ? or handle with map_err

findings.problem: parts[1].parse::<u32>().unwrap() panics on non-numeric or out-of-range input
findings.failure_mode: malformed CSV lines abort the program instead of returning a typed parse error
findings.fix: return Result<Vec<Record>, ParseError> and use ? on parse, handling the conversion to u16 with checked_into or try_from

findings.problem: as u16 is a lossy width cast that silently truncates values > 65535
findings.failure_mode: a valid u32 value like 70000 silently becomes 4448, corrupting data without any error
findings.fix: use u16::try_from(parsed_u32) or parsed_u32.checked_into::<u16>() and propagate the error

findings.problem: Uses split(','), .map().collect() + indexed access into Vec<String> instead of split_once for a known two-field record
findings.failure_mode: allocates an entire Vec of Strings for what is a two-field parse; extra allocations are unnecessary and the pattern invites unchecked indexing
findings.fix: use line.split_once(',') to get (name, value_str) directly, then trim and parse each field

findings.problem: parts[0] accesses Vec by index without bounds check
findings.failure_mode: empty or single-element lines cause a panic at runtime instead of returning a parse error
findings.fix: use split_once(',') which returns Option instead of panicking on short lines

findings.problem: parts[1] accesses Vec by index without bounds check
findings.failure_mode: lines with only one field cause a panic at runtime instead of returning a parse error
findings.fix: use split_once(',') which returns Option instead of panicking on short lines

findings.problem: println!() inside a function that should be a pure data loader; I/O (stdout) is mixed into the parsing logic
findings.failure_mode: side-effecting code in a data-loading function makes it non-deterministic, untestable in isolation, and couples parsing to stdout
findings.fix: remove println! from the core parsing path; if logging is needed, push it to a shell-level wrapper that calls the pure parser

findings.problem: load_sessions returns Vec<Record> with no bounded allocation handling; lines are collected into a Vec with no try_reserve
findings.failure_mode: large files can exhaust memory without a controlled allocation failure; Vec::with_capacity is not used and allocation errors are never handled
findings.fix: return Result<Vec<Record>, AllocationError>; use try_reserve on the Vec with a bounded capacity estimate and handle the allocation error

findings.problem: parse::<u32>() followed by as u16 uses unchecked arithmetic for width conversion; no checked_div or checked arithmetic is used anywhere
findings.failure_mode: silent truncation on values outside u16 range; no defensive checked operations for any arithmetic in the module
findings.fix: use u16::try_from() for the conversion and propagate errors via Result

findings.problem: No benchmark exists for load_sessions parsing performance
findings.failure_mode: no evidence that the allocation strategy (collect all lines into Vec, allocate Strings per field) is appropriate for the expected workload; performance is cargo-culted
findings.fix: add a criterion or divan benchmark measuring parse throughput and memory for typical input sizes

findings.problem: No profiler evidence (flamegraph, perf profile) to validate allocation hotspots in the parsing path
findings.failure_mode: the split + collect + clone pattern may be unnecessarily hot; without profiling it cannot be confirmed or refuted
findings.fix: run flamegraph or perf on a representative dataset to identify whether the String allocations in the parse loop are a real hotspot

findings.problem: No allocation tracking (e.g., dhat, heaptrack) to validate the allocation profile of the parsing pipeline
findings.failure_mode: unknown whether per-field String allocations dominate the allocation budget; could be reduced with borrowed &str until the final consumer
findings.fix: run an allocation profiler to measure per-record heap pressure; consider using &str for name with a lifetime or a single pre-allocated buffer

findings.problem: No dev-dependencies for testing or benchmarks; no benchmark framework, no criterion, no cargo-hack for MSRV testing
findings.failure_mode: no automated performance regression detection or MSRV gate exists for this crate
findings.fix: add [dev-dependencies] with criterion or divan for benchmarks; consider cargo-hack for MSRV matrix testing

missing_evidence: no benchmark exists for load_sessions parsing throughput and memory
no profiler evidence (flamegraph/perf) for the parsing allocation path
no allocation tracking (dhat/heaptrack) for the per-field String allocation strategy
no command evidence for cargo fmt, cargo clippy, or cargo test
residual_risk: Static review only; no commands run. The crate has 9 BLOCKER violations: unwrap() on I/O and parse (lines 9, 19), lossy as cast (line 19), unchecked indexing (lines 16, 19), split+collect+index instead of split_once (line 12), I/O side-effect in pure path (line 16), no try_reserve (line 8), no checked arithmetic (line 19). The function mixes imperative shell concerns (fs::read, println) with data parsing, and has no error type or Result return. All unwrap calls and lossy casts must be replaced with typed error propagation and checked conversions before delivery.
